title: landolphia madagascariensis
intro: Landolphia madagascariensis, commonly known as Poisonous Oleander or Madagascan Oleander, is a plant species native to Madagascar and other parts of Africa. It is a shrub or small tree that belongs to the Apocynaceae family, used in traditional medicine due to its numerous health benefits. The health benefits of Landolphia madagascariensis include its use in treating fever, rheumatism, and gastrointestinal issues, while its therapeutic actions involve anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of the plant include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
